title: Edit Distance
keyIdea: Compare word1[i] with word2[j]. Same letter → keep it, move both on for free. Otherwise try all three edits, each costing 1: insert word2[j] (j + 1), delete word1[i] (i + 1), replace word1[i] with word2[j] (both + 1), and keep the cheapest. Base: one word used up → insert or delete everything left in the other. Each cell needs only its right, below and diagonal neighbours, so two columns (or rows) are enough.

approaches.name: Recursion
approaches.idea: Match → solve(i + 1, j + 1); else 1 + min(insert, delete, replace).
approaches.why: Three branches on every mismatch with nothing saved; the stack is up to n + m deep.
approaches.warn: Too slow (TLE) for 500-letter words. Your comment about passing by reference is right: by value would copy both strings on every call.

approaches.name: Memoization
approaches.idea: Same recursion; save each (i, j) answer in dp.
approaches.why: n × m states with O(1) work each; dp table plus a stack up to n + m deep.

approaches.name: Tabulation
approaches.idea: Last row = m − col, last column = n − row. Fill i from n − 1 down and j from m − 1 down with the same rule. Answer dp[0][0].
approaches.why: Two nested loops; the whole table is kept.

approaches.name: Tabulation, two columns
approaches.idea: Your active code: j is the outer loop, so keep two columns indexed by i. next = column j + 1 (starts as n − i), curr = column j with curr[n] = m − j. Insert reads next[i], delete curr[i + 1], replace/match next[i + 1]. Answer next[0].
approaches.why: Same two loops; only two arrays of n + 1 (n = word1 length) are stored.

quiz.q: word1[i] ≠ word2[j]. Which state does 'insert word2[j]' lead to?
options: (i, j + 1): word2's letter is now matched, word1 hasn't moved
n − i: delete every letter left in word1

quiz.q: Why is a matching letter free (no + 1)?
options: Keeping the same letter needs no edit, and it's never worse than editing
Matches are counted at the end

quiz.q: In your two-column version, why is the space O(n) and not O(m)?
options: The outer loop is j, so the arrays are columns indexed by i (word1), of size n + 1
Because only the diagonal is stored
